provenance.notes: Care family batch. Health-adjacent and licensed: no medical or outcome claims, no invented family testimonials, licence and payment-programme wording as placeholders. Two buyers on one site: families and caregivers, so the hiring side is priced as seriously as the marketing side. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Companion care, personal care such as bathing and dressing, respite, overnight and live-in care, and dementia support as the agency provides it, with a plain note on what non-medical home care does not include
pageStructurePlus.why: Families arrive confused about the difference between home care and home health. The agency that explains it plainly earns the first call.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Pay range [as supplied], shift types, training provided, how scheduling works, the background check process and a short mobile application
pageStructurePlus.why: Caregiver hiring is the agency's constant bottleneck. A careers page that applicants can finish on a phone keeps shifts staffed.

pageStructurePlus.section: How caregivers are screened and matched
pageStructurePlus.contains: Background checks and references as the agency performs them, training topics, how a caregiver is matched on personality, language and schedule, and supervisor check-ins
pageStructurePlus.why: Letting a stranger into a parent's home is the decision. Families choose the agency that shows exactly how caregivers are chosen.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Private pay hourly rates and shift minimums, how the agency helps with long-term care insurance claims, and veterans or state programmes only where the agency states it takes part [as supplied]
pageStructurePlus.why: Cost is the question adult children ask first and the one most agencies hide. Explaining payment routes calmly keeps the family on the page.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How families receive visit notes, who the care coordinator is, how schedule changes are requested, and how a family in another city stays informed
pageStructurePlus.why: Many buyers are adult children living far away. Seeing how they'll stay informed is what lets them say yes from a distance.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Each town the caregiver team covers, shift minimums by area, and how quickly care can start in each
pageStructurePlus.why: Families search for home care in their parent's town, often far from their own. A clear coverage list answers the first filter.

designDirections.name: Kitchen Table
designDirections.bestFor: Small local home care agencies that need a clear phone number, a care request and a careers link above everything
designDirections.headlineSample: Home care for your parents in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Peach Sorbet's soft rounded type and warm ground feel like a kitchen-table conversation, and the split hero puts a real caregiver beside the call button.

designDirections.name: Trusted Agency
designDirections.bestFor: Established senior care agencies that need care levels, screening, payment routes and a serious careers section
designDirections.headlineSample: Senior care at home in {City}, explained plainly
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Sage Spa, fails CTA contrast. Evergreen Trust keeps the green calm, adds the credibility of an insurer-grade palette, and its buttons pass AA for older readers.

designDirections.name: Private Duty
designDirections.bestFor: Private-duty and live-in senior care agencies serving families who expect a concierge level of service
designDirections.headlineSample: Private home care in {City}, arranged personally
designDirections.whyItFits: Cacao's warm brown and bookish serif feel like a family home rather than a facility, and a full-bleed hero lets a quiet moment at home carry the page.

openers.line: Your agency's Maps listing has a phone number and no website, so a daughter in another state searching for home care for her mother in {City} can't see what you offer before deciding whom to call.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what could sit behind that button for the agency: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing opens the agency's Facebook page, mostly caregiver birthday posts. Families comparing senior care can't find care levels or a way to ask about starting.
openers.hook: Click the link on their listing. If it lands on Facebook, note what the latest posts are about.
openers.linkLine: The agency's care options on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: The home care site on your listing still shows a phone number that goes to voicemail and a careers link that's broken. Both families and caregivers hit that wall.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one stale or broken thing: careers link, old number, missing towns. Note it.
openers.linkLine: The same agency, current and working: {demo-link}

openers.line: I tried your agency site on my phone and the care request form wouldn't submit. Adult children usually look for home care from their phone, on a lunch break, worried.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Try the request form on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The agency, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts say you're always hiring caregivers, but the only way to apply is to call the office. Most caregivers job-hunt from their phone between shifts.
openers.hook: Look for 'now hiring caregivers' posts and check for an online application. If there isn't one, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A caregiver careers page they can finish on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Nothing online explains the difference between your companion care and personal care, or what you don't do. Families stall right there, and call the agency that explains it.
openers.hook: Check their site or listing for care level descriptions. If services are a bare list, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Levels of home care, explained plainly: {demo-link}

openers.line: One of your Google reviews describes a caregiver who learned exactly how a father liked his coffee. That's what a family hopes for, and it's not anywhere they'd read before calling.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about a caregiver's kindness or reliability. Quote it back. Never imply a health result.
openers.linkLine: Your reviews beside the care request: {demo-link}

openers.line: Over the holidays, adult children visit parents and notice things have changed. The week after, they search for senior care, and the agency with clear answers gets the call.
openers.hook: Use this in November and early December. Check whether they've posted about holiday family visits.
openers.linkLine: A home care page ready for the holiday conversation: {demo-link}

openers.line: Families decide on home care after a hospital discharge or a fall, often on a Friday night. Right now there's no way to request help until the office opens Monday.
openers.hook: Look for after-hours numbers or 'call anytime' claims. If there's only an office line, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: An agency page that takes care requests at any hour: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw your post looking for weekend caregivers in {Neighborhood}. Applicants check whether the agency looks organised before they trust it with their schedule.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a caregiver hiring notice. Note the date and the shifts mentioned.
openers.linkLine: A caregiver recruiting page for the agency: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing doesn't say which towns your caregivers cover. A family searching for senior care in their mother's town can't tell if you're even an option.
openers.hook: Check whether their service towns are listed anywhere. Use the real town names when you reply.
openers.linkLine: A home care page with every town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your agency doesn't mention cost or long-term care insurance anywhere online. That's the first thing adult children ask, and the most awkward to ask on the phone.
openers.hook: Look for rates, minimums or insurance mentions. Never state a programme they accept unless they say so.
openers.linkLine: Paying for home care, explained calmly: {demo-link}

openers.line: Nothing online says the agency is licensed or how caregivers are background-checked. Letting someone into a parent's home starts with exactly those two questions.
openers.hook: Look for licence or screening mentions on their profiles. Never state a licence number they haven't published.
openers.linkLine: Licensing and caregiver screening, shown plainly: {demo-link}

openers.line: It sounds like most of your clients come from discharge planners and senior living referrals. Families still look the agency up before agreeing, and find very little.
openers.hook: Look for posts about hospital partners or referral sources. Don't guess at their client base.
openers.linkLine: Where a referred home care family would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your post about {specific recent job} shows the kind of caregiver families hope for. That belongs on a page about how you match caregivers, not just the feed.
openers.hook: Pick their newest caregiver spotlight, training day or community event and name it exactly. Never a client's details.
openers.linkLine: That caregiver story, on the matching page: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, your post about {specific recent job} shows the kind of caregiver families hope for.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and only found the listing and social pages. I put together a sample agency page with care levels explained, a caregiver careers section families never see and applicants can finish on a phone, and a care request, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my message got buried. Here's the sample home care site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It explains care levels, shows how caregivers are screened and matched, covers paying for care, and has a caregiver application that works on a phone. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for home care agencies here in {City}. I sent a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Completely understand, scheduling never stops. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with care levels, a care request for families and a caregiver application, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and updates. For an agency like yours I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"Half of it works for hiring. Every caregiver who applies from a phone is a shift you can staff."
"Could I walk you through it for fifteen minutes this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: Our clients come from hospitals and referrals, not the internet.
objections.handler: "Then the site's job is to make the family comfortable after the referral, and to make the discharge planner look good for sending them. They all look the agency up."

objections.objection: Our biggest problem is hiring, not clients.
objections.handler: "That's why half the site is for caregivers. A careers page and an application that works on a phone help you staff the clients you already have."

objections.objection: The franchise gives us a page already.
objections.handler: "Keep it. If the brand allows a local page, I build one that names your towns, your caregivers and your office, within their rules."

objections.objection: We have to be careful what we promise families.
objections.handler: "Agreed. No health claims, no invented testimonials, and licence and payment wording only as you give it to me. You approve every page."
"That's your call. The payment page can explain shift minimums and insurance help without a number, and invite a conversation."
"{Build Range}. For your agency about {Build Price}, because of the careers side and the care pages. One family staying on care for a few months covers it."

email.subject: A site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for home care agencies in {City} and put together a sample for {Business Name}, including a caregiver careers page. I'll email the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm planning to take the {Business Name} agency demo down on Friday.

If you'd like it left up while you think, just reply and I'll keep it.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, the weeks after the holidays are when families who noticed changes in a parent start calling home care agencies, and when caregivers look for new work. Thought of you.

The sample is still here and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you'd like another look.

bullets: Peg the build to one family on care for a month or two. Hourly rates are low but care runs for months, and agencies know that maths.
Price the careers side as seriously as the family side. Hiring is the agency's real bottleneck.
Price town pages by area covered, not by count of zip codes.
Payment and licence wording stays as placeholders until the owner supplies it; charge for the structure, not invented facts.
Franchise locations are priced for what the brand allows locally, often less than a full build.
Keep monthly add-ons below the cost of a single caregiver shift.

lineItems.item: Caregiver careers page with mobile application
lineItems.description: Max with several job types, a mobile application, availability questions and routing to the hiring coordinator.
Max when the care level has its own what's-included list, what's not, and a request route.
Max with shift minimums, local start times and nearby hospitals or senior communities named as reference points.
Max with private pay, long-term care insurance help and programme pages the agency supplies wording for.

lineItems.item: Referral partner page for discharge planners
lineItems.description: Max with a referral form, start-of-care timing, coverage map and a downloadable one-page summary.

lineItems.item: Care request routing to the on-call coordinator
lineItems.description: Max when requests route by town and urgency to the right coordinator's phone after hours.
Max when family pages and the caregiver application are both translated and checked by bilingual staff.

whatElseYouSell.name: Caregiver team photo day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A morning photographing your caregivers, coordinators and office, with their consent, so families see real faces instead of stock pictures of smiling seniors."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, scheduled around a training day when caregivers are in the office.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for the home care agency
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Weekly updates on the agency's Google profile with towns served, caregiver spotlights and hiring posts, so both families and applicants find a current agency."

whatElseYouSell.name: Family review requests after the first month of care
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After a month of home care going well, the family contact gets a respectful note asking whether they'd share their experience."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 45. Wording approved by the agency, sent to the family contact only.

whatElseYouSell.name: Caregiver recruiting campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A month of hiring posts, a flyer for community boards and a referral bonus page, all pointing caregivers to the mobile application."
whatElseYouSell.when: Whenever they say they're turning down clients for lack of staff.

whatElseYouSell.name: Discharge planner and senior living outreach kit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page agency summary, a referral pad and a short email for discharge planners, social workers and senior living staff who send families your way."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the referral partner page is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Monthly family newsletter
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A calm monthly email for client families: caregiver spotlights, office news and seasonal home safety reminders the agency approves."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once family contacts are in one list.

whatElseYouSell.name: Vehicle magnets and caregiver badge artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Car magnets and ID badges with the agency name and careers code, so every caregiver's car in a driveway recruits the next caregiver."

withoutAI.route: Elder law attorneys who advise the same families
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The elder law attorney who sends families to your home care agency has a dated site. I build for careful, regulated offices already."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Elder law and home care share every family. The agency owner's introduction is the warm way in.

withoutAI.route: Senior move managers and downsizing specialists
withoutAI.whoPays: The move manager, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The senior move manager you work alongside books by phone and has no site. I'd build one with your agency listed as a partner."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Move managers meet families at the same turning point and refer to home care constantly.

withoutAI.whoPays: The contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The contractor who puts in grab bars and ramps for your clients needs a page showing those jobs. Families ask your caregivers who to call."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Caregivers see what a home needs and recommend the same contractor every time.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The adult day programme your clients attend twice a week fills spots by word of mouth. A site with a daily schedule and tour booking would help."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Day programmes and home care split the week for the same families and refer back and forth.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The school that trains the caregivers you hire enrols by flyer. A course site with dates and an application fills classes and your hiring pipeline."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: The agency is their best employer partner and vouches for you.

withoutAI.whoPays: The care manager, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The geriatric care manager who coordinates your clients' care for distant families has only a directory listing. A calm practice page is a quick build."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Care managers choose agencies for families. Helping them deepens the referral.

withAI.route: Intake logistics assistant for the elder law office
withAI.pitchLine: "Families asking the elder law office about consultation fees and documents to bring get approved answers, and legal questions are passed to a person."
withAI.whyItWorks: Law offices want after-hours intake without giving advice. Admin-only answers are the safe line.

withAI.route: Move planning helper for the senior move manager
withAI.pitchLine: "Families describe the move date and home size, and the move manager gets a draft plan and checklist from her own process, with home care partners listed."
withAI.whyItWorks: Move managers build plans by hand for every family. A draft saves them hours.

withAI.route: Job photo-to-quote drafts for the accessibility contractor
withAI.pitchLine: "A family sends pictures of the bathroom and front steps, and the contractor gets a draft scope for grab bars or a ramp from their own price list."
withAI.whyItWorks: Accessibility jobs start with a site visit. Draft scopes from pictures save trips.

withAI.route: Tour and enrolment assistant for the adult day programme
withAI.pitchLine: "Families asking about the adult day programme's schedule, transport and fees get answers from its own handbook and can book a tour."
withAI.whyItWorks: Day programmes answer the same questions from every family. A contained assistant books tours.

withAI.route: Enrolment question assistant for the caregiver school
withAI.pitchLine: "People thinking about becoming caregivers ask about class dates, cost and job placement and get answers from the school's own pages."
withAI.whyItWorks: More enrolments means more caregivers for the home care agency to hire. Everyone wins.

withAI.route: Family update drafts for the geriatric care manager
withAI.pitchLine: "The care manager's notes become a clear weekly update draft for the distant family, which she reviews and sends from her own secure system."
withAI.whyItWorks: Care managers spend evenings writing family updates. A draft they control saves that time.

softwareAI.name: Applicant first-reply texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A caregiver who applies at nine at night gets a text within minutes with interview times, before another home care agency calls them first."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 14, as soon as the careers page is live. Needs the hiring coordinator's interview calendar and wording.

softwareAI.name: After-hours care request routing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A family's Friday-night request for home care reaches the on-call coordinator's phone with the town and start date, not Monday's inbox."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: At build or day 14. Needs the on-call rota and town list. Collects contact and needs summary only, no medical history.

softwareAI.name: Applicant pipeline board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every caregiver applicant in one place: applied, interviewed, background check, training, first shift, so nobody falls through the cracks."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their hiring steps and the people who move applicants along.

softwareAI.name: Caregiver job question responder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants asking about pay, shifts, towns and requirements get answers from the agency's approved careers page at any hour, and a link to apply."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs approved pay and shift wording. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: After-hours phone answering for families
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Calls from worried families after the office closes get answered with the agency's care levels and towns, a coordinator call-back booked, and any emergency directed to emergency services."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once they trust you. Needs care levels, coverage and the owner's escalation wording. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Privacy-safe review reply drafts for the agency
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each home care review gets a warm reply drafted for approval that never mentions the client's health or confirms details about their care."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Family enquiry follow-up
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A family who asked about senior care but didn't start gets a gentle check-in a week later, and one more a month later, then nothing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the enquiry list and approved wording.

softwareAI.name: Open shift text-out to available caregivers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A caregiver calls out sick, and every available caregiver in that town gets a text with the shift; the first to accept is confirmed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs caregiver availability and towns, kept separate from client details. Works alongside their scheduling system.

softwareAI.name: Caregiver onboarding checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each new caregiver's documents, background check status and training steps tracked on one checklist until their first home care shift."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their onboarding steps and the state's required documents as the agency lists them.

softwareAI.name: Caregiver referral bonus tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Caregivers who refer a friend see when the bonus is earned, and the office stops tracking it on sticky notes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, if they run a referral bonus. Needs the bonus rules.

softwareAI.name: Home care hours cost estimator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Families enter how many hours a week of care they're thinking about and see a range from the agency's own rates and minimums, with a call to talk it through."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, only if the owner agrees to show ranges. Needs their hourly rates and shift minimums.

softwareAI.name: Care needs conversation guide
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A family describes daily routines their parent needs help with, and the coordinator receives a tidy summary and a suggested care level to discuss, never a health assessment."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the agency's care level definitions and coordinator review of every summary. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Caregiver refresher quiz drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The agency's own training material becomes short monthly refresher quizzes for caregivers, drafted for the trainer to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the agency's written training material. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Bilingual caregiver message drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Schedule changes and office notices to caregivers are drafted in English and Spanish from one message the coordinator writes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, for agencies with Spanish-speaking caregivers. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Coordinator handbook search
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New care coordinators search the agency's own policies on call-outs, client starts and family requests instead of interrupting the owner."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the written office handbook, every answer approved. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Family visit summary drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Caregiver visit notes become a short weekly summary for the distant family, reviewed by the coordinator before it's sent through the agency's secure system."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7, only inside their secure system with family consent. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Recruiting source report
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which job posts, referrals and flyers bring caregivers who actually reach a first shift, and stop paying for the ones that don't."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, once the applicant pipeline has a few months of data.

softwareAI.name: Caregiver anniversary and recognition messages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Caregivers get a thank-you from the owner on their work anniversary and after a hundred home care visits. Small things keep good people."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs start dates and the owner's wording.

softwareAI.name: Family updates page linked to their secure system
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Families log in from the agency site to see upcoming caregiver visits and coordinator contacts, pulled from the agency's existing secure system."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8, only if their scheduling system allows a secure link. Needs their vendor's access and a privacy review.

softwareAI.name: Multi-office numbers board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "For owners with a second home care office: enquiries, starts, applicants and caregiver hours side by side, in totals only."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, when they open a second office. Needs summary exports from both.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the caregiver recruiting kit for independent agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a mobile caregiver application, first-reply texts and an applicant board for one home care agency. Every agency is short of caregivers."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Hiring is the universal pain in home care. A recruiting kit sells without a website conversation.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your franchisees each need a local careers page and town pages inside brand rules. I build an approved template once."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Franchise systems sell territories and need each one staffed. Local recruiting pages are an easy approval.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: State home care association member toolkit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member agency a site template with care levels, screening and careers pages built in, free of health claims."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need member benefits, and compliant marketing and hiring are top concerns.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Partner agency directory for a hospital discharge team
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your discharge planners hand families a photocopied list of home care agencies. A searchable directory by town and care level helps families decide faster."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Hospitals need safe, quick discharges. The agency client is already one of their partners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Senior living communities adding home care
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your community is adding in-home care for residents and neighbours. It needs its own care levels and careers pages, which I've already built for an agency."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Communities expanding into home care don't know the copy or hiring setup. You do.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Families call your office to find senior care providers by town. A plain-language resource directory answers that around the clock."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Public agencies have budget for access tools, and the home care client is a provider on their list.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label home care template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your marketing agency picks up home care clients and builds generic sites. License my template with care levels and a caregiver careers flow built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell the part that hires caregivers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your policyholders ask which home care agencies near them help with claims. A partner page by town makes your service more useful."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Brokers want policyholders to feel looked after. A vetted agency list helps them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Graduate job boards for caregiver training networks
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every graduate of your caregiver courses needs a first job. A job board with local agencies hiring fills your placement promise."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Training networks sell placement. Agencies pay to reach graduates.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each home care agency you acquire comes with a different site. I move them onto one template with local careers and town pages intact."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Roll-ups need consistent brands fast, and they buy in batches.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New home care clients in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Home care agencies outside {City} don't serve the same families as mine, so they get the same care levels, careers and payment pages."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The slow parts, careful wording and the hiring flow, carry straight over.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Someone started your home care site and left the careers page unfinished. I can finish it on an agency setup I've already shipped."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stuck agencies already budgeted the work and need caregivers now.

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention turning down a family because no caregiver was available.
upsellLadder.line: "A family you couldn't staff is a recruiting problem. Let's fill the caregiver pipeline."

upsellLadder.trigger: Applicants are being tracked in a spreadsheet or a text thread.
upsellLadder.line: "Your caregiver applicants deserve better than a text thread. Let's track them to the first shift."

upsellLadder.offer: Discharge planner and senior living outreach kit
upsellLadder.trigger: They say most new home care clients come from hospital referrals.
upsellLadder.line: "Your home care referral page is live. Let's put it in front of every discharge planner nearby."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention weekend calls from families going to voicemail.
upsellLadder.line: "Families calling about home care on a Saturday get a calm answer and a coordinator call-back."

upsellLadder.offer: Open shift text-out to available caregivers
upsellLadder.trigger: A coordinator describes spending a morning calling caregivers to cover one call-out.
upsellLadder.line: "That morning of phone calls to cover one caregiver shift can be a single text."

upsellLadder.offer: Introduction to the elder law attorney
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention an elder law attorney who refers families and asked who built the site.
upsellLadder.line: "The elder law attorney who sends you families asked about the site. Would you introduce me?"
